name: hash_cracker
description: Crack a hash you are authorised to crack, offline, on this machine. Identifies a hash by shape, converts a capture file into hashcat's modern WPA mode 22000 (or the older hccapx), lists the wordlists this machine already has, and starts a hashcat or John session that reports back its real speed and progress. Every crack runs on a file that is already here: no hash is uploaded, no server is contacted, and a missing tool is named with the package that provides it.

operation.description: One of: tools | identify | convert | crack | john | status | wordlists | sources. Defaults to tools.

hash.description: The hash to identify, or its first characters.

hash_file.description: Path to a hash file (.hc22000, .hccapx, a raw hash per line) for cracking, converting or status.

capture.description: Path to an existing .cap/.pcap capture to convert into a crackable hash.

wordlist.description: Wordlist path. When omitted, hashcat runs in increment mode and says so.

mode.description: hashcat mode number, e.g. 22000 for WPA-PBKDF2-PMKID+EAPOL, 0 for MD5, 1000 for NTLM. Defaults to 22000.

rules.description: Optional hashcat rule file name, e.g. best64.rule.

workload.description: hashcat workload profile 1-4. Defaults to 2, which is honest about not locking up the desktop.

confirm.description: Must be true to start a cracking session. Defaults to false (nothing runs).

limit.description: Maximum entries to return. Defaults to 20.

author: Stella
notes: External tools: hashcat (mode 22000), john, hcxpcapngtool, cap2hccapx, aircrack-ng. Probed per call. Cracking is offline-only and only ever targets a file that already exists on this machine.
